Palestine White and Black.author: Paul Von Blum
Palestine White and Black.quote: This collection features many achingly powerful works that capture the pain of the daily life of ordinary Palestinians.

Palestine White and Black.author: Sarah Rose Sharp
Palestine White and Black.quote: His images hyper-literalize the struggle of Palestinians to remain vital and connected to their homeland under conditions designed to crush their existence.

Palestine White and Black.author: Marguerite Dabaie
Palestine White and Black.quote: These political cartoons are foremost a form of solidarity with ordinary Palestinians in their daily struggle for survival and ongoing battle for justice.

Raw, gut-wrenching visualisations that claw at the senses with their depiction of families torn apart, prisoners crushed by injustice and despair that life outside is simply another version of the prison.

Palestine White and Black.author: Ramona Wadi
Palestine White and Black.quote: An intense communication of Palestinian life; bludgeoned, displaced, yet still resisting.
Many just speak for themselves, with a powerful voice that deserves to be widely heard.
Readers of the book will find themselves drawn time and again to each of its pages, noticing new details and hidden symbolism upon each viewing.

Palestine White and Black.author: Karie Firoozmand
Palestine White and Black.quote: A story of violence, anguish, loss, and trauma but also of precious connections, shared resilience, and intractable resistance.

Palestine White and Black.author: Ramona Wadi
Palestine White and Black.quote: Sabaaneh’s cartoons are multi-layered and compel the viewer to approach them comprehensively in context.

Palestine White and Black.author: John Stang
Palestine White and Black.quote: Sabaaneh’s style also calls to mind a grim black-and-white-and-gray mix of Picasso and Gahan Wilson.

Palestine White and Black.author: Ahmad Melhem
Palestine White and Black.quote: Mohammad Sabaaneh, Palestine’s controversial caricaturist, has published a book with his cartoons that has been collecting awards at home and abroad.

Power Born of Dream.quote: Sabaaneh presents a world in which injustice is unending, but so is the strength of his people.
An excellent account of life under Israeli occupation, along with credible information to support the author’s point of view and claims.

Power Born of Dream.author: Omar Ahmed
Power Born of Dream.quote: Sabaaneh’s trademark black and white blend of expressionist and surrealist artwork with its Kafkaesque and exaggerated style depicting the emotive Palestinian experience under Israeli occupation.

Power Born of Dream.author: Rita D. Jacobs
Power Born of Dream.quote: The stark black-and-white linocut images are as harsh and as powerful as the narrative, and the unadorned, straightforward language drives the emotions home.
Although this is clearly a book about real things and real lives at stake, it is distinguished and animated by its magic realist elements and expressive art work.

Power Born of Dream.author: Tjeerd Royaards
Power Born of Dream.quote: This is a book that deserves a broad international audience.

Power Born of Dream.author: Terry Weber
Power Born of Dream.quote: As usual Sabaaneh’s art work is incredibly evocative.

Power Born of Dream.source: Washington Report on Middle East Affairs
Power Born of Dream.quote: Sabaaneh helps us see that the prison is much larger than a building, far wider than a cell; it stretches through towns and villages, past military checkpoints and borders.

Power Born of Dream.author: Paul Buhle
Power Born of Dream.quote: This is a review about two outstanding comics.

Power Born of Dream.author: Jean Stern
Power Born of Dream.quote: Cet oiseau-là survole et raconte un monde d’enfermement et d’oppression qui est celui de la Palestine depuis des décennies.

Power Born of Dream.author: Bernie Gourley
Power Born of Dream.quote: I enjoyed the art and found this to be an interesting read, but I wouldn’t recommend readers take it at face value as a fair account of the conflict.

Power Born of Dream.author: Jorge Sanchez
Power Born of Dream.quote: Œuvre émouvante d’un artiste ayant fait ses armes dans le dessin de presse.
Les éditions Le Fennec publient la traduction du dernier roman graphique de Mohammad Sabaaneh, «Je ne partirai pas, mon histoire est celle de la Palestine».

Welcome to hell.author: Sean Dillon
Welcome to hell.quote: [Sabaaneh’s] more surrealistic stylings instead present the true horror being experienced day in and day out within Palestine with the depth and honesty it deserves.

Welcome to hell.author: Paul Von Blum
Welcome to hell.quote: Mohammad Sabaaneh documents the specific contours of life amid this type of genocide powerfully and unnervingly.

Welcome to hell.author: Kevin Brown
Welcome to hell.quote: The imagery of mirrors and seeing (or not seeing) carry throughout the work to show a broader view of imprisonment in both the West Bank and Gaza, especially how nobody wants to see Palestinians as human.

Welcome to hell.author: Kate
Welcome to hell.quote: Sabaaneh doesn’t waste a page and has a lot of important and devastating things to say, and does so effectively.

Welcome to hell.author: Tom Smithyman
Welcome to hell.quote: The book is incredibly powerful, frightening beyond belief, and still somewhat hopeful.

Welcome to hell.author: Steven Heller
Welcome to hell.quote: It is a story of displacement, starvation and attack.

Welcome to hell.author: Frank Plowright
Welcome to hell.quote: Welcome to Hell is so disappointing for being an opportunity to shine a light on abhorrent behaviour, and while rightful anger is present, it seems more concerned with form over content.

30 second from Gaza.quote: By freezing these moments so beautifully in time, Sabaaneh refuses to let readers look away.

30 second from Gaza.author: Andy Oliver
30 second from Gaza.quote: 30 Seconds from Gaza is one of the most difficult books you will read this year, and for that very reason I urge you to do just that.

30 second from Gaza.author: Ramona Wadi
30 second from Gaza.quote: Mohammad’s Cubist drawings in this collection occupy a unique place in memory, making them hard to forget.

30 second from Gaza.author: Pina Fioretti
30 second from Gaza.quote: “30 Seconds From Gaza” è un’opera che trasporta artisticamente l’esperienza devastante vissuta dall’autore Mohammad Sabaaneh e dall’intero popolo palestinese.
